title: introduce-triangle-evictor-and-occupancy-align-allocator-to-reduce-kv-fragmentation
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: In production KV workloads we observed long-tail memory amplification caused by small, heterogeneous slot allocations and conservative eviction scoring. This PR introduces two coordinated components: (1) an occupancy-align allocator that reduces internal fragmentation by biasing allocations into a small set of triangular size bins and (2) the Triangle Evictor — a three-axis eviction heuristic that blends recency, occupancy-impact, and size-gradient to choose victims more robustly under mixed workloads.

Design summary: The allocator groups allocation sizes into triangular buckets (bins whose boundaries follow a geometric progression with controlled overlaps); new allocations prefer the lowest-overhead bin that satisfies alignment constraints. The allocator exposes a lightweight occupancy hint per tenant/shard used by the evictor. The Triangle Evictor computes a composite score = w_recency*recency_score + w_occ*occupancy_impact + w_size*size_gradient. occupancy_impact estimates how much contiguous free space will be recovered if an item is evicted (favoring items that unblock larger coalesced regions). size_gradient penalizes tiny allocations that would worsen fragmentation if kept. The evictor also integrates a spillover gate: when physical memory pressure crosses a soft-threshold, large cold regions are asynchronously compacted and spilled to the configured backing store via a low-priority spill worker.

Compatibility & safety: Runtime feature-flag guarded (kv.triangle_evictor.enabled=false by default). Evictor falls back to previous LRU-ish policy on mismatch, and the allocator supports a compatibility mode that preserves previous bucket boundaries. All code paths respect tenant isolation quotas and the existing accounting metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] allocator implementation and unit tests
- [x] evictor algorithm + integration tests
- [x] async spill worker and backpressure controller
- [x] metrics and trace points for eviction decisions
- [x] perf harness runs and benchmark artifacts attached
- [x] feature flag gating and k8s config knobs for private/dedicated deployments

Notes: This is focused on memory-management/eviction; it intentionally does not change continuous-batching or kernel selection code. Follow-ups will include an optional compaction pass in the continuous-batcher hot path and a tenant-aware prefetch when spilled pages are rehydrated.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (review): Can you add a short explanation of the geometric progression constants and why overlaps are necessary? Also please document worst-case CPU overhead when eviction rate spikes.

Aisha Patel (author): Added section to docs and comments in triangle_allocator.rs explaining bin growth factor and overlap rationale; worst-case CPU path is limited by a rate-limited evictor loop and we bound per-iteration candidate checks to 64 entries (documented).
Leah Chen (review): We saw a small regression in a tight 99th p99 latency microbenchmark with tiny-alloc-dominant workload. Can we make occupancy_impact weight configurable by tenant?
Aisha Patel (author): Made occupancy weight tenant-configurable via kv.tenant_defaults.eviction_weights. Benchmarks included in PR updated to show improvement when tuned per-tenant.
Omar Siddiqui (review): Please ensure spill worker obeys disk QoS and doesn't impact critical IO lanes in dedicated deployments.
Aisha Patel (author): Spill worker uses the platform IO QoS token bucket and falls back to a background queue; added integration test that simulates IO contention.
release_notes: Introduces Triangle Evictor and Occupancy-Align allocator (opt-in via kv.triangle_evictor.enabled). Reduces memory fragmentation and lowers average eviction churn under mixed-size workloads. Config knobs: kv.allocator.bin_growth, kv.eviction_weights, kv.spill.soft_threshold, kv.spill.rate_limit.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover allocator bin placement, overlap edge cases, and evictor scoring. Integration tests validate tenant quotas and fallbacks. Perf harness: ran against three workloads (small-alloc churn, mixed-sizes, large cold objects) in the internal benchmark lab. CI runs exercised cross-platform builds (x86/arm) and the spill worker tests ran on a simulated backing store. All CI checks passed.
perf_results:
Benchmarks (internal harness, median of 5 runs):
- Small-alloc churn workload: memory amplification reduced from 2.3x -> 1.25x, eviction rate down 48%, p99 latency +2% (config-tuned per-tenant eliminated regression).
- Mixed-size throughput workload: throughput +6-9% and 95th token latency -12%.
- Large-object workload with async spill: peak RSS lowered 28% and spill I/O bandwidth stayed within configured rate limits.
Detailed CSV artifacts uploaded to perf/harness/artifacts/pr-631942/
